text:
Arturs Silovs has had a rough fall in Pittsburgh. He is 5-7-1 with an .873 save percentage, and he has allowed 3.0 more goals than his shots would usually produce (36th percentile). Over his last five starts that hole is 4.52 goals deep, including six allowed to Boston on Nov. 5.

The problem is specific. On low-danger shots he has been fine, .982 against a league .963. On high-danger chances he is at .656 against .687, in the bottom 4% of goalies, and on medium-danger shots he is giving away 2.54 goals. Those are the saves that decide close games, and his 5-7-1 record shows it.

There is history here too. Last season he finished 12.8 goals below expected in 39 games by our model, though Evolving-Hockey had him slightly positive, so the two systems disagree about how bad that was. Our talent range puts his true level a touch below league average. He is 25, a Latvian Olympian who once carried his country at the 2023 World Championship, and the next month decides whether he holds a starter's share.
headline: Silovs is losing on the hard ones
